history: At the meeting of the Roshi and Punyamati rivers, the medieval complex grew around Indreshwor Mahadev Temple, traditionally dated to 1294. It also includes the 17th-century Brahmayani Temple and historic rest houses. Nepal submitted the complex to UNESCO’s Tentative List in 1996.

history: Sankhu dates to the Lichchhavi period and stood on an old trade route to Tibet. Nepal’s Department of Archaeology dates the hill’s main Bajrayogini temple complex to the mid-17th century. Nepal submitted the town and temple together to UNESCO’s Tentative List in 2008.
